title: HMAC accumulation buffer has no size cap
description: Complexity: accumulation buffer doubles per Update, allocating O(total HMAC input). For TLS record MACs (max ~16 KB per record) this is fine. For bulk HMAC (e.g., file integrity check with wc_HmacUpdate over a 100 MB file), the buffer allocates 100 MB on the heap silently. With WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_POOL_SIZE=8 in-flight HMACs of 1 GB each, this allocates 8 GB. The comment at port.c:1019-1026 says 'use a second devId that skips HMAC offload for bulk data' — but there is no max-size guard, no error, and no diagnostic when the buffer grows large. Impact at scale: OOM on servers that accidentally route bulk HMAC through this port. Fix: add a compile-time cap (e.g., WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF, default 64KB) and return CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE when the cap is exceeded.
